Agent Integration API

Install Blog GitHub

Agent Integration API

Gollek exposes an agent-facing serving contract for systems such as Wayang-Gollek. The API lets an external agent runtime discover serving capabilities, validate payloads, fetch MCP tool definitions, create embeddings, inject caller-selected RAG context, and call OpenAI-compatible generation endpoints.

Gollek does not plan, execute tools, own memory, or manage workflow state. Those decisions stay in Wayang-Gollek or another agent orchestrator.

Endpoint Summary

Purpose Method Path Model Invoked
Capability discovery GET /v1/agent/capabilities No
Machine-readable contract GET /v1/agent/contract No
Readiness issue catalog GET /v1/agent/readiness/issues No
Serving preflight POST /v1/agent/preflight No
Request validation POST /v1/agent/validate?surface={surface} No
Tool schema validation POST /v1/agent/tools/validate No
MCP server discovery GET /v1/mcp/servers No
MCP tool discovery GET /v1/mcp/tools?compat=openai No
Chat Completions POST /v1/chat/completions Yes
Responses POST /v1/responses Yes
Embeddings POST /v1/embeddings Yes
Model capabilities GET /v1/models/{id}/capabilities No

Use GET /v1/agent/contract as the source of truth for the current schema hints. The current contract object uses version: "v1", contract_version: "v1", supported_contract_versions: ["v1"], and service_role: "inference_serving_engine".

Auth And Trace

Deployments can expose API-key and authorization headers according to the returned contract. The Java SDK sends Gollek trace headers through AgentRequestOptions. For compatibility with Gollek’s serving endpoints, the SDK sends both X-API-Key: <token> and Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Field Header Body aliases
Request id X-Gollek-Request-Id request_id
Trace id X-Gollek-Trace-Id trace_id, trace
Session id X-Gollek-Session-Id session_id, conversation, previous_response_id
User id X-Gollek-User-Id user, user_id

Gollek propagates trace details into response headers and response metadata under gollek_trace.

Contract Discovery

Use capabilities for lightweight feature discovery:

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/agent/capabilities \
  -H "X-API-Key: community"

Use the contract endpoint when an orchestrator needs endpoint paths, schema hints, boundary rules, streaming metadata, and trace behavior:

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/agent/contract \
  -H "X-API-Key: community"

The contract includes:

  • contract_version
  • supported_contract_versions
  • compatibility
  • feature_negotiation
  • boundary.gollek_owns
  • boundary.agent_orchestrator_owns
  • auth
  • traceability
  • streaming
  • endpoints
  • schemas
  • readiness_issue_catalog
  • readiness_issue_catalog_by_code

Wayang-Gollek should read these fields at startup or during health checks, then adapt its own workflow only to supported surfaces. Use feature_negotiation.required_features as the startup gate for a Wayang-Gollek integration. Treat unknown feature names as forward-compatible and ignore them unless your orchestrator explicitly needs that feature. Gollek keeps the feature flags scoped to serving primitives such as OpenAI-compatible chat/responses, embeddings, MCP tool discovery, request validation, tool contract validation, and RAG context injection; Wayang-Gollek still owns planning, memory, retrieval policy, vector-store state, tool authorization, tool execution, retries, and workflow state. The readiness issue catalog gives non-Java clients the same stable code, default severity, summary, and remediation metadata that the Java SDK exposes through AgentReadinessIssueCodes. For clients that only need code metadata, call GET /v1/agent/readiness/issues instead of downloading the full contract.

Serving Feature Profiles

Feature profiles are named shortcuts for serving requirements. They help an orchestrator request a known Gollek capability bundle without hardcoding every feature flag. Profiles still describe serving primitives only; they do not choose an agent plan, execute tools, select documents, own memory, or create workflow state.

feature_negotiation.default_feature_profile is agent_serving. The contract also returns supported_feature_profiles and a feature_profiles catalog with each profile’s required and optional features.

Profile Use it for Still owned by Wayang-Gollek or caller
agent_serving Full serving gate for chat, Responses, embeddings, MCP discovery, validation, and RAG context injection Planning, memory, retrieval policy, vector store, tool execution
chat_agent Chat Completions serving with tools, system prompts, streams, and caller-supplied RAG context Agent loop, tool authorization, tool execution, retrieval
responses_agent Responses API serving with the same external orchestration boundary Agent loop, tool authorization, tool execution, retrieval
embedding_rag Embedding generation for caller-owned RAG indexing and retrieval Chunking policy, vector storage, retrieval, ranking
mcp_tools MCP discovery plus tool schema validation without execution MCP calls, auth, approvals, tool result loop

Send feature_profile to /v1/agent/preflight when a route has a known shape. If required_features or optional_features are supplied, they override the profile-derived lists for that request. Unsupported profile names block the feature-negotiation check with FEATURE_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED.

Model Route Capabilities

Use model capabilities before routing a particular agent request. This endpoint describes whether a selected model can use Gollek’s serving surfaces for system prompts, tools, streaming, embeddings, and caller-supplied RAG context. Gollek advertises this route as model_capabilities in both /v1/agent/capabilities and /v1/agent/contract; treat it as a required preflight surface for agent-serving integrations.

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models/demo-model/capabilities \
  -H "X-API-Key: community"

From the CLI, use the same model-route check and fail CI when the selected model cannot satisfy the agent-serving route:

gollek agent model-capabilities \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --model demo-model \
  --require-serving-boundary

The capability matrix includes:

  • available, known, preferred_provider
  • limits
  • api_contract
  • openai_compatibility
  • inference
  • tooling
  • rag
  • embeddings
  • modalities
  • provider_candidates
  • metadata

For an agent-serving route, require completion serving, Chat Completions and Responses compatibility, system prompt support, tool definition ingestion, and RAG context injection. Also keep tooling.tool_execution, rag.retrieval_policy, and rag.vector_store_ownership set to false so Wayang-Gollek remains responsible for tool execution and retrieval policy.

For embedding and RAG indexing routes, require openai_compatibility.embeddings, modalities.embeddings, and embeddings.generation. Use embeddings.dimensions to match a caller-owned vector store when model metadata knows the output size, and treat embeddings.encoding_formats plus embeddings.input_aliases as the stable request-shape hints. The embedding capability block must keep embeddings.retrieval_policy and embeddings.vector_store_ownership set to false; Gollek generates vectors, while Wayang-Gollek or another orchestrator owns retrieval and storage.

Serving Preflight

Use server-side preflight when a non-Java client wants one validation-only readiness report instead of calling every discovery endpoint itself. The preflight combines capabilities, contract, feature negotiation, selected model route, MCP discovery, tool contract validation, and request validation. The response also echoes contract_version, supported_contract_versions, and feature_negotiation, so CI can store one artifact that records which serving contract was checked. Send required_contract_version, required_features, and optional_features to make that negotiation explicit. Unsupported required features block the preflight; unsupported optional features become warnings.

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/agent/preflight \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: community" \
  -d '{
    "model": "demo-model",
    "surface": "chat",
    "feature_profile": "chat_agent",
    "required_contract_version": "v1",
    "required_features": ["rag_context", "mcp_tool_discovery"],
    "optional_features": ["stream_usage_reporting"],
    "request": {
      "request_id": "req_preflight_123",
      "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": "Use supplied context."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Can this route support my agent?"}
      ],
      "tools": [
        {
          "type": "function",
          "function": {
            "name": "search_context",
            "parameters": {"type": "object"}
          }
        }
      ],
      "rag_context": [
        {"source": "docs", "text": "Gollek validates readiness without invoking the model."}
      ]
    }
  }'

The CLI exposes the same server-side preflight for local development and CI:

gollek agent capabilities \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --require-serving-boundary

gollek agent contract \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --require-serving-boundary

gollek agent issue-catalog \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --area tool_validation \
  --require-serving-boundary

gollek agent model-capabilities \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --model demo-model \
  --require-serving-boundary

gollek agent tools-validate \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --tool-file tools.json \
  --require-clean \
  --require-serving-boundary

gollek agent request-validate \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --model demo-model \
  --surface chat \
  --prompt "Can this route support my agent?" \
  --tool-file tools.json \
  --rag-context "Gollek validates payload mapping without invoking the model." \
  --require-clean \
  --require-serving-boundary

gollek agent mcp-tools \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --require-tools \
  --require-serving-boundary

gollek agent readiness \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --model demo-model \
  --surface chat \
  --feature-profile chat_agent \
  --prompt "Can this route support my agent?" \
  --rag-context "Gollek validates readiness without invoking the model." \
  --require-tools \
  --require-clean \
  --require-serving-boundary \
  --json

gollek agent preflight \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --model demo-model \
  --surface chat \
  --feature-profile chat_agent \
  --preflight-policy requested_route \
  --prompt "Can this route support my agent?" \
  --rag-context "Gollek validates readiness without invoking the model."

Use gollek agent template-schema --json to print the canonical Draft 2020-12 schema for saved route templates before wiring a builder, GitHub Action, or Wayang-Gollek integration. Use gollek agent template-example --list to inspect the starter catalog first, or gollek agent template-example --list --json when a website or builder UI needs machine-readable route choices. Use gollek agent template-example --id embedding_rag --output wayang-agent-route.json to emit a valid starter route by catalog id for chat, Responses, embeddings/RAG, or MCP tool-schema routes, then run it through template-check before publishing. Human mode prints the exact gollek agent template-check --request-file ... --json command for the saved file, including shell-safe quoting when the path contains spaces. Use --json when stdout must remain machine-readable, or combine --output with --list to save the catalog JSON for a local builder cache. Output writes are conservative by default and require --overwrite before replacing an existing file. The id flag accepts the catalog ids and normalizes hyphenated aliases such as embedding-rag; explicit surface or feature-profile overrides must match the selected id. Use gollek agent template-check --request-file wayang-agent-route.json --json as the local publishing guard when CI only needs to parse a saved route template and catch top-level/nested route drift. It returns object: "gollek.agent_template_check" and exits without HTTP, model invocation, tool execution, retrieval, or workflow state. It also rejects missing model ids, unsupported surfaces, unsupported feature profiles, and preflight policy typos before a low-code builder publishes the template. JSON output keeps the compatibility issues string array and adds issue_details[] with stable code, field, optional value, optional suggested_value, and optional allowed_values so GitHub Actions or builder UIs can annotate the exact setting and display likely fixes for common typos. Human output prints the same stable codes plus compact field, value, suggested-value, and allowed-value hints for template issues. Use gollek agent readiness as the CI bundle when an orchestrator wants one local command to call every discovery and validation surface. It returns object: "gollek.agent_readiness_report" with checked_areas, checks, issues_by_area, and per-check results for capabilities, contract, model capabilities, MCP tools, tool validation, request validation, and server preflight. Use --json for raw discovery, readiness, preflight, or issue-catalog responses. gollek agent issue-catalog --area tool_validation prints the stable code, default severity, summary, and remediation metadata that dashboards can show when preflight returns active issues. gollek agent capabilities, gollek agent contract, gollek agent issue-catalog, gollek agent model-capabilities, gollek agent tools-validate, gollek agent request-validate, and gollek agent mcp-tools exit 1 with --require-serving-boundary when the server, selected model, or validation response drifts from the inference-serving boundary. gollek agent readiness always fails on blocked checklist items, including boundary drift, because it is meant to be a complete agent-serving gate. gollek agent tools-validate --require-clean, gollek agent request-validate --require-clean, and gollek agent readiness --require-clean also exit 1 on portability warnings; gollek agent mcp-tools --require-tools and gollek agent readiness --require-tools exit 1 when discovery returns no usable tools. gollek agent template-check, gollek agent request-validate, gollek agent readiness, and gollek agent preflight accept --feature-profile with the same serving profile names advertised by the contract. embedding_rag defaults generated CLI requests to the embeddings surface when --surface is omitted. gollek agent preflight accepts --request-json or --request-file for a full OpenAI-compatible request, and --no-mcp for routes that do not depend on MCP discovery. template-check exits 0 when the saved template is locally valid, 1 when the template itself is invalid, and 2 for CLI parse/config errors. The readiness and preflight commands exit 0 when the route is ready, 1 when blocked, and 2 for local CLI or connection errors.

Preflight Policies And Route Gates

Server preflight reports whether Gollek can serve a request. The caller still chooses how strict the integration gate should be. Use a policy profile when Wayang-Gollek, another agent runtime, or CI needs the same decision every time.

Policy profile Blocks on Use it for
readiness_only Gollek readiness failures only Local development and loose compatibility checks.
requested_route Readiness failures plus selected route mismatch Production startup checks where model, surface, and feature profile must stay stable.
clean Readiness failures, route mismatch, and warnings CI, release gates, and low-code agent publishing checks.

The CLI also exposes the strictness switches directly:

  • --require-route-match blocks when the selected route differs from the requested model, surface, or feature profile.
  • --fail-on-warning or --fail-on-warnings blocks when preflight returns warnings.
  • --preflight-policy clean is equivalent to requiring route match and failing on warnings.

Examples:

gollek agent preflight \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --model demo-model \
  --surface chat \
  --feature-profile chat_agent \
  --preflight-policy readiness_only

gollek agent preflight \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --model demo-model \
  --surface chat \
  --feature-profile chat_agent \
  --preflight-policy requested_route

gollek agent preflight \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --request-file wayang-agent-route.json \
  --preflight-policy clean \
  --json

--json returns a typed wrapper with object: "gollek.agent_preflight_result". It preserves the raw server response, the typed readiness report, the requested route, the selected route, route_comparison, route_mismatches, route_mismatch_messages, preflight_gate, and preflight_policy. The raw server response remains object: "gollek.agent_preflight".

When the selected route drifts from the request, route_comparison.mismatches and top-level route_mismatches show each field with requested, selected, and a compact message. This is the first place to inspect when CI blocks on requested_route or clean.

Request files can carry their own baseline policy, which the CLI can make stricter with flags:

{
  "model": "demo-model",
  "surface": "chat",
  "feature_profile": "chat_agent",
  "preflight_policy": {
    "profile": "requested_route"
  },
  "request": {
    "model": "demo-model",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Use supplied context and tools when relevant."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Answer using the provided context."}
    ],
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "search_context",
          "parameters": {"type": "object"}
        }
      }
    ],
    "rag_context": [
      {"source": "docs", "text": "The agent runtime selected this context before calling Gollek."}
    ]
  }
}

Use this shape for low-code builders and agent templates: the template can ask for requested_route, while CI can add --preflight-policy clean before publishing. The policy never executes tools, runs retrieval, stores memory, or chooses the next agent step; it only decides whether Gollek’s serving route is acceptable for the caller.

Keep the top-level route fields and nested request route fields aligned. For example, top-level model, surface, and feature_profile should match any nested request.model, request.surface, and request.feature_profile. The gollek agent template-check, gollek agent request-validate, gollek agent readiness, and gollek agent preflight fail locally on explicit conflicts before calling Gollek. Use --model, --surface, or --feature-profile when a CI job or operator intentionally wants to override a saved template. With --json, local route conflicts emit code: "AGENT_ROUTE_CONFLICT" and a conflicts array containing field, top_level, and request values, so CI can report exactly which saved-template route field drifted.

The response always keeps the serving boundary visible:

  • object: "gollek.agent_preflight"
  • status: "ready" or "blocked"
  • ready
  • blocking_issue_count
  • warning_count
  • ready_check_count
  • blocked_check_count
  • skipped_check_count
  • check_results
  • checked_areas
  • readiness_report
  • issues
  • issue_hints
  • issue_hints_by_area
  • issue_hints_by_code
  • remediation_plan
  • blocking_remediation_plan
  • warning_remediation_plan
  • remediation_plan_by_area
  • remediation_plan_by_code
  • issues_by_area
  • issue_codes_by_area
  • blocking_messages
  • warning_messages
  • blocking_codes
  • warning_codes
  • boundary.validation_only: true
  • boundary.model_invoked: false
  • boundary.tool_execution: false
  • boundary.retrieval_execution: false

Use check_results when a CI job or agent dashboard needs per-area status for capabilities, contract, model route, MCP discovery, tool validation, and request validation. Each check includes status, ready, requested, blocking_messages, warning_messages, blocking_codes, warning_codes, issue_hints, remediation_plan, and remediation_plan_by_code; status: "skipped" with requested: false means the preflight intentionally did not run that area. Use the top-level and per-check code fields for automation, and the message fields for operator-facing logs. The top-level issues array carries the same stable code per issue, alongside area, severity, and message; issue_codes_by_area, blocking_codes, and warning_codes provide compact summaries for CI gates and dashboards. issue_hints adds default_severity, summary, and remediation for active issues so non-Java dashboards can show operator guidance without reimplementing the SDK catalog. issue_hints_by_area and issue_hints_by_code expose the same active hints grouped for dashboards, CI annotations, and orchestrator health checks. remediation_plan deduplicates those active hints into next-action steps with the source messages preserved. blocking_remediation_plan and warning_remediation_plan expose the same steps split by severity for CI gates, while remediation_plan_by_area keeps the same steps grouped by readiness area and remediation_plan_by_code groups them by stable readiness code. For all possible readiness codes, read readiness_issue_catalog or readiness_issue_catalog_by_code from GET /v1/agent/contract, or call the lighter GET /v1/agent/readiness/issues endpoint. Checks can also include details for typed dashboard summaries. Embedding preflights expose check_results.request_validation.details.embedding with input counts, input lengths, requested dimensions, encoding format, metadata keys, and the embedding/RAG ownership boundary. The contract exposes this shape through schemas.agent_preflight_check_result so clients can validate each check_results entry consistently.

Human-mode gollek agent preflight and gollek agent readiness print the same details as operator-facing lines. Readiness also echoes the selected feature profile beside the model and surface. Blocking and warning messages include stable [code: ...] annotations when codes are available. When a code maps to the readiness issue catalog, the CLI also prints a short remediation: line from issue_hints or the SDK catalog. Treat these lines as a readable projection of the JSON check_results and issue_hints maps, not as a separate contract:

Selected route: model=other-model, surface=chat, feature_profile=chat_agent
Route comparison: mismatch fields=model
  mismatch: model requested=demo-model selected=other-model
Preflight gate: blocked
  blocking: selected route differs from requested route: model requested=demo-model selected=other-model

- request_validation: ready, requested=true
  details: surface=chat, model=demo-model
  boundary: validation_only=true, model_invoked=false, tool_execution=false, retrieval_execution=false
  request: streaming=false, messages=2, inputs=0, tools=1, parameters=model,tools
  rag: injected=true, items=1, alias=rag_context

For embedding preflights, the request-validation detail line exposes the vector route without giving Gollek retrieval or storage ownership:

- request_validation: ready, requested=true
  details: surface=embeddings, model=demo-embed
  embeddings: inputs=2, input_lengths=5,4, requested_dimensions=768, encoding=float, metadata_keys=tenant
  embedding boundary: generation=true, retrieval_execution=false, retrieval_policy_owner=agent_orchestrator, vector_store_owner=agent_orchestrator

The contract schema advertises check_results as a map keyed by readiness area so clients can validate future areas without hard-coding a fixed field list. The top-level response and nested readiness report both include checked_areas, ordered like the emitted checks map, so dashboards can show which preflight stages were evaluated without expanding each check. readiness_report mirrors the CLI/SDK gollek.agent_readiness_report shape while the top-level object remains gollek.agent_preflight for backward-compatible API callers. The contract marks emitted trace, boundary, check-count, issue, and message fields as required for both the top-level preflight response and the nested readiness report.

By default, preflight requires MCP discovery, tool validation, and request validation. For routes that do not use MCP tools, set discover_mcp_tools: false, mcp_discovery_required: false, and optionally validate_tools: false.

For embedding-only RAG indexing checks, preflight the embedding route without MCP/tool checks:

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/agent/preflight \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: community" \
  -d '{
    "model": "demo-embed",
    "surface": "embeddings",
    "discover_mcp_tools": false,
    "mcp_discovery_required": false,
    "validate_tools": false,
    "tool_validation_required": false,
    "request": {
      "request_id": "req_embed_preflight_123",
      "input": ["Find context for this task"],
      "dimensions": 768,
      "encoding_format": "float",
      "metadata": {"tenant": "agent-project"}
    }
  }'

The resulting model_capabilities.embeddings block reports whether /v1/embeddings can generate vectors for the selected model, known dimensions, accepted encoding formats, input aliases, and the retrieval/vector-store boundary. The nested request_validation.normalized block reports input_count, input_lengths, requested_dimensions, encoding_format, and rag.vector_store_owned_by: "agent_orchestrator" without invoking the model. For CI and dashboards, the same summary is available at check_results.request_validation.details.embedding.

Readiness uses the same request-building flags as preflight, plus --no-tool-validation, --no-request-validation, --mcp-optional, and --no-mcp when a route intentionally skips part of the checklist. It does not execute tools, run retrieval, authorize tools, or invoke a model; it only verifies that Gollek is ready to serve the request while the agent runtime owns planning and workflow state.

Request Validation

Validation maps a request without invoking a model. Use it before a workflow starts or when a low-code builder saves an agent configuration.

curl -s "http://localhost:8080/v1/agent/validate?surface=chat" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: community" \
  -d '{
    "model": "demo-model",
    "request_id": "req_validate_123",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Use supplied context."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Validate this request."}
    ],
    "rag_context": [
      {"source": "docs", "text": "Gollek validates agent-facing payloads."}
    ]
  }'

Supported validation surfaces are chat, responses, and embeddings. From the CLI, validate generated or supplied request JSON directly:

gollek agent request-validate \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --model demo-model \
  --surface chat \
  --prompt "Validate this request." \
  --tool-file tools.json \
  --rag-context "Caller-owned retrieval context." \
  --require-clean \
  --require-serving-boundary

Use --request-json or --request-file when validating a real agent builder payload. The command accepts either a direct request object or a full saved route template with a nested request object, checks route consistency locally, then posts only to /v1/agent/validate; it does not invoke a model, execute tools, run retrieval, or update agent memory.

The validation response reports:

  • object: "gollek.agent_validation"
  • surface
  • valid
  • model_invoked: false
  • normalized
  • trace
  • boundary.validation_only: true
  • boundary.tool_execution: false
  • boundary.retrieval_execution: false

Tool Contract Validation

Gollek accepts OpenAI-compatible tool definitions and MCP-derived tool definitions, validates their schema shape, and can return tool-call declarations from model output. Gollek does not authorize or execute tools.

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/agent/tools/validate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: community" \
  -d '{
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "search_context",
          "description": "Search caller-owned knowledge",
          "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "query": {"type": "string"}
            },
            "required": ["query"]
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }'

Tool validation is useful for Wayang-Gollek low-code builders because invalid tool definitions can be rejected before a workflow is published. From the CLI, validate a tool bundle directly and optionally fail CI on portability warnings:

gollek agent tools-validate \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --tool-file tools.json \
  --require-clean \
  --require-serving-boundary

The command posts only to /v1/agent/tools/validate; it does not invoke a model, authorize a tool, execute a tool, or start an agent loop.

MCP Discovery

Gollek can expose registered MCP servers and tool definitions:

curl -s "http://localhost:8080/v1/mcp/tools?compat=openai" \
  -H "X-API-Key: community"

Use compat=openai when the next call is /v1/chat/completions or /v1/responses.

From the CLI, discover OpenAI-compatible MCP tool definitions and fail CI if the MCP surface is unavailable, crosses into execution, or returns no tools:

gollek agent mcp-tools \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --require-tools \
  --require-serving-boundary

Use --server <name> to inspect one MCP server, --raw-mcp-tools for raw MCP tool schemas, and --include-disabled-mcp when diagnostics need disabled registrations.

Gollek’s role ends at discovery and schema conversion. Wayang-Gollek owns the MCP client loop, tool authorization, execution, result messages, retries, and operator approval.

Embeddings For Caller-Owned RAG

Gollek generates embeddings, but the vector store and retrieval policy belong to the caller.

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: community" \
  -d '{
    "model": "demo-embed",
    "request_id": "req_embed_123",
    "trace_id": "trace_embed_123",
    "input": ["Find context for this task"],
    "metadata": {"tenant": "agent-project"}
  }'

OpenAI-compatible embedding responses contain object: "list", model, data[].embedding, and metadata. SDK callers can use AgentEmbeddingView to extract vectors, dimensions, usage, metadata, and trace details.

Use POST /v1/agent/validate?surface=embeddings when a builder or CI job needs to dry-run the request shape before serving. The normalized validation payload reports input_count, input_lengths, optional requested_dimensions, encoding_format, metadata, and a RAG boundary summary showing that retrieval execution, retrieval policy, and vector-store ownership remain outside Gollek.

RAG Context Injection

After Wayang-Gollek retrieves and ranks documents, pass selected chunks to Gollek as rag_context.

Accepted aliases include:

  • rag_context
  • retrieval_context
  • retrieved_context
  • context_documents
  • retrieved_documents

Context items can include:

Field Purpose
text, content, page_content Retrieved text chunk
id, chunk_id Stable chunk id
source URI, file, path, or source label
title Human-readable title
score Retriever relevance score
metadata Caller-owned metadata

Gollek injects supplied context into the model request and records RAG metadata. It does not search a vector store or choose which documents are relevant.

Chat Completions

Use Chat Completions for OpenAI-compatible message arrays:

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: community" \
  -d '{
    "model": "demo-model",
    "request_id": "req_agent_123",
    "trace_id": "trace_agent_123",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "Answer using supplied context and tools when relevant."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "What changed for agentic support?"}
    ],
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "search_context",
          "parameters": {"type": "object"}
        }
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "rag_context": [
      {
        "id": "chunk-1",
        "source": "docs/agentic",
        "score": 0.92,
        "text": "Gollek exposes inference APIs for agent orchestrators."
      }
    ]
  }'

For streaming, set stream: true and use stream_options:

{
  "stream": true,
  "stream_options": {
    "include_usage": true,
    "include_trace": true,
    "include_stream_metadata": true
  }
}

Streaming uses server-sent events and ends with data:[DONE].

Responses

Use Responses when the caller prefers instructions, input, previous_response_id, and Responses-compatible stream events.

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/responses \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: community" \
  -d '{
    "model": "demo-model",
    "instructions": "Use the provided context when relevant.",
    "input": "Summarize the Gollek agent integration boundary.",
    "retrieval_context": [
      {
        "source": "docs/api",
        "text": "Gollek owns serving, MCP discovery, embeddings, and RAG context injection."
      }
    ],
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "lookup",
          "parameters": {"type": "object"}
        }
      }
    ]
  }'

Responses streaming emits events such as response.created, response.output_text.delta, response.output_text.done, and response.completed, then the [DONE] sentinel.

Java SDK Bridge

The full Java remote SDK exposes the same serving boundary through client.agent(). Standalone agent runtimes can also depend on the lighter gollek-sdk-agent artifact and construct AgentIntegrationClient directly. Use servingReadiness(...) when a caller wants the SDK to run discovery and dry-run validation as one serving-only preflight. Use the individual typed views when a UI needs to display each contract section separately. Non-Java runtimes can call POST /v1/agent/preflight directly for the same readiness shape.

AgentRequestOptions trace = AgentRequestOptions.builder()
    .requestId("req-wayang-123")
    .traceId("trace-wayang-123")
    .sessionId("session-abc")
    .userId("user-42")
    .build();

AgentCapabilitiesView capabilities = client.agent().capabilitiesView(trace);
if (!capabilities.hasRequiredAgentServingCapabilities()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Gollek capabilities mismatch: "
        + capabilities.agentServingCapabilityIssues());
}

AgentServingContract contract = client.agent().contractView(trace);
if (!contract.hasRequiredServingBoundary()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Gollek serving boundary mismatch: " + contract.servingBoundaryIssues());
}

AgentModelCapabilitiesView model = client.agent().modelCapabilitiesView("demo-model", trace);
if (!model.hasRequiredAgentServingRoute()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Model cannot serve this agent route: "
        + model.agentServingRouteIssues());
}

AgentModelCapabilitiesView.EmbeddingCapabilities embeddingRoute = model.embeddings();
if (!embeddingRoute.storageOwnedByOrchestrator()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Embedding route crossed the RAG storage boundary");
}

AgentMcpDiscoveryView tools = client.agent().mcpToolsView(true, true, trace);
if (!tools.discoveryOnly()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("MCP discovery endpoint crossed the serving boundary");
}

AgentToolValidationView toolCheck = client.agent().validateToolsView(
    Map.of("tools", tools.openAiToolDefinitions()), trace);
if (toolCheck.hasWarnings()) {
    wayangAudit.recordToolSchemaWarnings(toolCheck.warnings());
}

AgentEmbeddingView embedding = client.agent().createEmbeddingView(Map.of(
    "model", "demo-embed",
    "input", List.of("Find context for this task")
), trace);

List<Map<String, Object>> retrievedChunks = wayangVectorStore.search(embedding.firstVector());

Map<String, Object> chatRequest = Map.of(
    "model", "demo-model",
    "messages", List.of(
        Map.of("role", "system", "content", "Use supplied context and tools when relevant."),
        Map.of("role", "user", "content", "Answer the task.")),
    "tools", tools.openAiToolDefinitions(),
    "rag_context", retrievedChunks
);

AgentValidationView dryRun = client.agent().validateRequestView("chat", chatRequest, trace);
if (!dryRun.validationOnly() || dryRun.modelInvoked()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Validation endpoint crossed the serving boundary");
}

AgentServingReadinessReport readiness = AgentServingReadinessReport.builder()
    .capabilities(capabilities)
    .contract(contract)
    .modelRoute(model)
    .mcpDiscovery(tools, true)
    .toolValidation(toolCheck, true)
    .requestValidation(dryRun, true)
    .build();
readiness.requireReady("Gollek serving preflight failed");
wayangAudit.recordPreflight(readiness.toReport());
if (readiness.hasWarnings()) {
    wayangAudit.recordPreflightWarnings(readiness.warningMessages());
}

AgentResponseView response = client.agent().createChatCompletionView(chatRequest, trace);

wayangToolLoop.handle(response.toolCalls());
wayangMemory.recordAssistantMessage(response.outputText());

Compact preflight callers can use:

AgentServingReadinessReport readiness = client.agent().servingReadiness(
    "demo-model",
    "chat",
    chatRequest,
    trace);
readiness.requireReady("Gollek serving preflight failed");

When the Gollek server exposes POST /v1/agent/preflight, Java callers can use the same one-call server-side preflight and still receive the typed readiness report:

AgentServingReadinessReport readiness = client.agent().servingPreflightReadiness(
    AgentServingPreflightRequest.builder()
        .modelId("demo-model")
        .surface("chat")
        .featureProfile("chat_agent")
        .request(chatRequest)
        .requestOptions(trace)
        .build());
readiness.requireReady("Gollek serving preflight failed");

Use the typed result and gate when the caller also wants route-match and warning policy in one reusable object:

AgentServingPreflightPolicy policy = AgentServingPreflightPolicy.requestedRoute();

AgentServingPreflightResult result = client.agent().servingPreflightResult(
    AgentServingPreflightRequest.builder()
        .modelId("demo-model")
        .surface("chat")
        .featureProfile("chat_agent")
        .request(chatRequest)
        .requestOptions(trace)
        .build());

AgentServingPreflightGate gate = result.gate(policy);
if (!gate.ready()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Gollek serving gate failed: "
        + gate.blockingMessages());
}

wayangAudit.recordPreflightGate(gate.toMetadata());

For the shortest SDK call, ask the client to evaluate the policy directly:

AgentServingPreflightGate gate = client.agent().servingPreflightGate(
    AgentServingPreflightRequest.builder()
        .modelId("demo-model")
        .surface("chat")
        .featureProfile("chat_agent")
        .request(chatRequest)
        .requestOptions(trace)
        .build(),
    AgentServingPreflightPolicy.clean());
gate.result().readiness().requireReady("Gollek serving preflight failed");
if (!gate.ready()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Gollek route gate failed: "
        + gate.blockingMessages());
}

AgentServingPreflightPolicy.readinessOnly() checks only server readiness, requestedRoute() also requires the selected route to match the request, and clean() also treats warnings as blocking. AgentServingPreflightResult exposes requestedRoute(), selectedRoute(), routeMatches(), routeMismatchFields(), routeMismatches(), routeMismatchDetails(), routeMismatchMessages(), readyForRequestedRoute(), and statusForRequestedRoute() for dashboards and integration tests.

toReport() emits the same CI-friendly shape as the CLI readiness gate: object: "gollek.agent_readiness_report", readiness status, blocking and warning counts, check counts, per-check messages, and the validation-only boundary. Use toMetadata() when the agent runtime only needs compact status fields to attach to request metadata; the metadata includes checked_areas for compact health dashboards. SDK callers can also use blockingCodes(), warningCodes(), issueCodesByArea(), and per-check helpers such as requestValidationCheck().hasBlockingCode("AGENT_REQUEST_INVALID") for CI gates or agent-runtime routing decisions. readiness.issueHints() returns active issues with catalog summaries and remediation text; AgentReadinessIssueCodes.describe(code) returns the same catalog metadata for standalone codes. Readiness checks can also include details; for embedding preflights, checks.request_validation.details.embedding contains input counts, input lengths, requested dimensions, encoding format, metadata keys, and the embedding/RAG ownership boundary.

For a non-MCP route, keep the same serving checks while skipping MCP discovery and tool validation:

AgentServingReadinessReport readiness = client.agent().servingReadiness(
    AgentServingPreflightRequest.builder()
        .modelId("demo-model")
        .surface("chat")
        .request(chatRequest)
        .requestOptions(trace)
        .discoverMcpTools(false)
        .mcpDiscoveryRequired(false)
        .validateTools(false)
        .build());
readiness.requireReady("Gollek serving preflight failed");

For embedding-only routes, pass surface("embeddings"). The SDK then validates the selected model through embeddingRouteIssues() instead of requiring chat, tool, and RAG-context generation features:

AgentServingReadinessReport readiness = client.agent().servingReadiness(
    AgentServingPreflightRequest.builder()
        .modelId("demo-embed")
        .surface("embeddings")
        .request(Map.of(
            "model", "demo-embed",
            "input", List.of("Find context for this task"),
            "dimensions", 768,
            "encoding_format", "float"))
        .requestOptions(trace)
        .discoverMcpTools(false)
        .mcpDiscoveryRequired(false)
        .validateTools(false)
        .toolValidationRequired(false)
        .build());
readiness.requireReady("Gollek embedding route is not ready");

The request dry-run also exposes typed embedding details, which is useful when Wayang or another orchestrator wants to verify dimensions, encoding, and RAG ownership before it creates vectors:

AgentValidationView dryRun = client.agent().validateRequestView(
    "embeddings",
    Map.of(
        "model", "demo-embed",
        "input", List.of("Find context for this task"),
        "dimensions", 768,
        "encoding_format", "float"),
    trace);

AgentValidationView.EmbeddingValidation embedding = dryRun.embeddingValidation();
if (!embedding.rag().embeddingGeneration()
        || embedding.rag().retrievalExecution()
        || !embedding.storageOwnedByOrchestrator()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Gollek crossed the embedding/RAG serving boundary");
}

wayangAudit.recordEmbeddingDryRun(Map.of(
    "dimensions", embedding.requestedDimensions(),
    "encoding_format", embedding.encodingFormat(),
    "input_lengths", embedding.inputLengths()));

For live agent UIs or coding-agent loops, the lightweight bridge can also stream without adding reactive dependencies:

AgentStreamAccumulator.Snapshot stream = client.agent().streamChatCompletion(
    Map.of(
        "model", "demo-model",
        "messages", messages,
        "tools", tools.openAiToolDefinitions(),
        "rag_context", retrievedChunks),
    trace,
    event -> {
        if (event.hasDelta()) {
            wayangUi.appendDelta(event.delta());
        }
        if (event.hasToolCalls()) {
            wayangToolLoop.preview(event.toolCalls());
        }
    });

wayangToolLoop.handle(stream.toolCalls());
wayangMemory.recordAssistantMessage(stream.outputText());

In this bridge, Gollek produces embeddings, validates contracts, serves the model, and returns tool-call declarations. Wayang-Gollek owns vector search, tool execution, memory updates, approval policy, and the next agent step.

For a runnable version of this flow, use the JBang example in the Gollek repo:

cd gollek
./gradlew smokeJbangAgentBridgeExamples -Pgollek.jbang.agentBridge.offline=false

To run the script manually:

./gradlew :sdk:gollek-sdk-agent:publishToMavenLocal
cd examples/jbang
jbang run --no-integrations integration/wayang_gollek_serving_bridge.java --mock

Use --live --base-url http://localhost:8080 --api-key community when a Gollek serving endpoint is running.

Wayang-Gollek Recipe

  1. Start a Wayang-Gollek workflow with request, trace, session, and user identity.
  2. Call GET /v1/agent/capabilities, GET /v1/agent/contract, and optionally GET /v1/agent/readiness/issues during startup or health checks.
  3. Run POST /v1/agent/preflight or call each discovery endpoint separately.
  4. Check the selected route with GET /v1/models/{id}/capabilities.
  5. Load MCP tools from Gollek using GET /v1/mcp/tools?compat=openai.
  6. Validate low-code tool definitions with POST /v1/agent/tools/validate.
  7. Generate an embedding with POST /v1/embeddings.
  8. Search the Wayang-Gollek vector store using the embedding vector.
  9. Pass selected chunks to Gollek as rag_context.
  10. Call /v1/chat/completions or /v1/responses.
  11. If Gollek returns tool calls, execute them in Wayang-Gollek.
  12. Send tool results back through a follow-up generation call if the workflow needs another model step.
  13. Store memory, audit events, approvals, and workflow state in Wayang-Gollek.

Non-Goals

Gollek’s agent integration API intentionally does not:

  • Plan tasks.
  • Execute tools.
  • Authorize tool calls.
  • Own memory.
  • Choose retrieval policy.
  • Store vector indexes.
  • Manage workflow state.
  • Render low-code agent builders.
  • Run multi-agent coordination loops.

Those responsibilities belong in Wayang-Gollek or another external orchestrator.
